doom.driver: UK PM says RAF base incidents ‘likely coordinated’ by Iran. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham says the incidents at RAF Fairford and RAF Molesworth were likely coordinated by Iran.
doom.blurb: UNINVITED GUESTS AT THE BOMBER BASE
doom.summary: Britain now says Iran was likely behind incidents at two RAF bases tied to US air power, while Hormuz crews are being paid danger money just to sail through and Houthi missiles keep arriving in Saudi Arabia. Trump's 'energy ceasefire' lasted about as long as it took Russia to hit six more Ukrainian energy sites, and Washington is buying Russian diesel anyway. Ethiopian troops are in Adwa, India has trimmed 130 million names off its voter rolls, and someone hacked the fridges in French supermarkets, because even the yogurt isn't safe.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: Meta's Muse Wonder rejoins the frontier and Microsoft's Maia 300 chip loosens Nvidia's grip, so the race keeps speeding up.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: Immigration agents searched a sitting congresswoman's home, feds used fake cell towers on journalists, and India's voter purge has sent protesters to the Supreme Court.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Iran-linked plots on UK bases, Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, attacks on Hormuz shipping, Russia hitting Ukrainian gas sites and Ethiopia pushing into Tigray add up to fires on several fronts at once.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: Meta advertises guardrails to keep its agents from going off the rails, an industry admission that going off the rails is a live option.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: A record-strength El Niño revives memories of the 1870s famines, while a Pentagon breach exposing about 3 million records and the supermarket fridge hack keep the cyber front busy.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing — a flat Gloucestershire field at dusk just outside the perimeter fence of RAF Fairford, the Cotswold horizon a thin black line beneath a huge sky burning blood-orange at the bottom and fading to deep black overhead, volcanic underlighting rising from the horizon so everything in the foreground falls into hard silhouette, cool tones nearly extinguished. Wet grass and a muddy lane glint with orange reflections. In the middle distance, a double chain-link fence topped with coils of razor wire runs across the frame, with a floodlight mast and a guard hut as black cutouts. Beyond the fence, the unmistakable silhouette of a B-52 bomber sits on the apron with its long drooping wings and paired engine pods, backlit by the glowing sky. In the foreground, two figures stand in silhouette on the lane at the fence line: an older man in a flat cap and waxed jacket with a dog at his feet, and a young woman beside him clutching a camera against her chest. Both are frozen and looking toward the base, shoulders slumped, the woman's hand half-raised to her mouth. Beside them a leaning stone wall and a tiny village church spire on the far left edge anchor the English setting. A single small blue-black police car with a dim orange-tinted light bar waits at the far gate. The faint trace of a drone-shaped speck hangs in the upper sky, barely visible. The mood is quiet dread, with the event implied and never shown.

dawn.driver: British adventurer returns home after 28-year walk around the world. Adventurer Karl Bushby swam the English Channel and celebrated with fish and chips after his 28-year, 30,000-mile walk from Chile to England.
dawn.summary: Karl Bushby set out from the southern tip of Chile, walked 30,000 miles, swam the English Channel and finally reached England 28 years later, where he marked it with a plate of fish and chips. Few people ever finish a journey of that size, and he did it on his own two feet. Elsewhere, NASA captured Australia's red outback bursting into what may be its richest wildflower bloom in nearly 20 years, and Judge Judy's Her Honor program celebrated two decades of mentoring young women.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: Researchers found that restoring a protein called Menin reversed several signs of aging in older mice within 30 days, and a new skin cream lowered skin's biological age by about two years in just four weeks.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: Apple is working with Indigenous communities to put endangered languages on the iPhone keyboard, so young speakers can type in their ancestral tongues every day.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: Karl Bushby completed a 28-year, 30,000-mile walk from Chile to England, finishing one of the longest unbroken journeys on foot in human history.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: Unusually heavy rains turned Australia's rust-colored outback into a vast carpet of wildflowers, and NASA photographed it from space.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: Owen Hanna celebrated his 100th birthday at his favorite bowling alley in Pennsylvania, still rolling in his happy place.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. NIGHT SCENE inside a small terraced-house kitchen in Hull, England. Deep indigo shadows fill the corners and the ceiling, and every bit of light comes from artificial sources. A brass-based table lamp with a fresh-green glass shade casts a pool of golden-yellow light over a worn wooden table. A porch lamp glows amber through a rain-speckled window, and the dark street beyond has one streetlight and a few fallen autumn leaves. On the table lies an open newspaper whose front page is a large map graphic with one bright golden line winding across continents, from the bottom of South America up through frozen seas to a small marked dot on the English coast, with only gray pixel blocks for headlines. Beside it sits a paper-wrapped portion of golden battered fish and thick chips with a bright green scoop of mushy peas, still steaming in the lamplight. A birthday card showing two tiny cartoon soldiers is propped against a teapot, and a small Union Jack tea towel hangs from the oven door. By the back door, a pair of well-worn walking boots waits on a mat, and an empty chair with a folded cardigan is pulled up to the table. The mood is quiet, steady and warm, with golden-yellow and fresh-green highlights against the dark.
